issue_context.title: Improve documentation on ActionListener#delegateFailure
issue_context.body:
the use of [ActionListener#delegateFailure](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/2517d5c065a03d409f55806dc1c97bfb80146b66/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/action/ActionListener.java#L98-L100) is [basically to define a lambda that's called on ActionListener#onResponse](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/2517d5c065a03d409f55806dc1c97bfb80146b66/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/action/ActionListenerImplementations.java#L204-L216). It doesn't have much to do with failure handling, per se: delegateFailure() passes `this` in to set `delegate`.

One can say that it delegates the onFailure handler while allowing override of the onResponse handler. It would be easier to understand if renamed (and re-documented) to reflect its purpose to override the onResponse handling.

Documentation should also be added for how [DelegatingFailureActionListener](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/9a7c62453f2be3d6627cfbeae505e8ed4544bc0f/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/action/ActionListenerImplementations.java#L200) works, to explain why #delegateFailureAndWrap doesn't use it, while #deleteFailure does.

-----------------

It would also be great to extend the documentation on [ActionListener#wrap](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/2517d5c065a03d409f55806dc1c97bfb80146b66/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/action/ActionListener.java#L161-L164) that recommends using `ActionListener#delegateFailure*` if the onFailure remains unchanged. There's no explanation why #delegateFailure is a better choice. The reason can likely be discerned from https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/96575, but it isn't obvious at a glance.

review_comments: Discussing child classes doesn't explain what this class does (also layer violation). The child classes themselves explain the differences well enough.

These child classes pre-date `SubscribableListener` by many years, and did not have this common superclass until quite recently, so I think it's useful to mention them here for the sake of folk that know the children but not the parent.
https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/96575 seems to have been about performance, but I can't easily discern the particulars to note here.
I would guess it's (some subset of) avoiding the allocation of the method reference, reducing the layers of wrapping, and being easier for the compiler to spot and optimise the pattern.
